scope: Repository safety review of a prior K2 experiment; no experiment or slot used
hypothesis: B1+B2: Hidden Great Basin faults share the local multi-physics expression (magnetic/gravity potential-field edges, topographic break, basement-depth step, conductivity contrast at 150-600 m scales) of catalogue faults, learnable from the 19-band GeoDAWN stack without any catalogue-derived predictor; fault tips continue beyond mapped segment ends. Emitting the learned surface as binary dots (min separation 2.8 px, 1.10% budget, >2 px off the known catalogue) maximizes distance-weighted Tversky credit per dot on hidden faults.
mechanism: HistGradientBoosting classifier (350 iterations, lr 0.06, 63 leaves, min-leaf 40, L2=1.0) on 26 features (14 raw bands + gradient magnitudes at sigma 1.5/4.0 px for rtp, det_elev, iso_grav, depth_to_base, cond_surf + 2 difference-of-Gaussians), fit per holdout fold on visible catalogue positives vs sampled unlabeled pixels >3 px from visible faults; tip-continuation corridors (visible components >=15 px, PCA strike, <=25 px, x2 surface boost); greedy descending-surface dot emission with 2.8 px minimum separation. Shared gems57-pooled-hide-v2 evaluator, label-blind quadrant whole-component folds, 8 km buffer, visible faults masked pixel-exactly in scoring.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic/intrusive contacts produce identical potential-field steps; alluvial-fan terrace risers and Lahontan shorelines mimic scarps; mapped-catalogue bias means the model learns 'faults that get mapped', which may differ systematically from the expert-hidden set (missing-not-at-random).
